subject.note: race is not an input feature

claims.statement: The demographic parity gap between the two race groups is at most 0.10.

audit.method: demographic parity difference on held-out individuals

assumptions: The audit sample is drawn from the same population the claim is about.
Group membership is known to the auditor.
The decision threshold is the one the claim was made at (0.5).
interference: Training the same model with DP-SGD changes this gap; see results/interference_privacy.csv.

claims.statement: The demographic parity gap between the two race groups is at most 0.25.

audit.method: demographic parity difference on held-out individuals

assumptions: As above, with a threshold inside the audit's own band.

subject.note: trained by plain SGD: no robustness or privacy protection of any kind

claims.statement: Accuracy under L-infinity attacks of size 0.1 is at least 0.30.
assumptions: The attack is the strongest one the auditor ran; a stronger attack can only lower the number (see results/robustness_strength.csv).
The claim is specific to this attack size: the same model reports 0.86 at size 0.02 and 0.35 at size 0.1.
interference: Adversarial training raises this number, and also strips the privacy audit below of most of its power: the epsilon it can rule out falls from 2.0 to 0.0 as the training radius grows, which is a loss of detection and not a gain in privacy. See results/interference_robustness.csv.

claims.statement: The training procedure satisfies differential privacy with epsilon at most 1.

audit.method: canary membership test, Clopper-Pearson lower bound on epsilon

assumptions: This audit can only lower-bound epsilon: passing it is evidence of nothing more than the audit's own limited power.
The model under audit here was trained with NO privacy protection, so its true epsilon is unbounded.
interference: Raising the DP noise multiplier costs 2 points of clean accuracy but takes robust accuracy from 0.28 to 0.00, so a robustness claim verified before privacy hardening does not survive it. See results/interference_privacy.csv.
This audit's power depends on how the model was trained, so its number cannot be compared across pipelines.

On an adversarially trained model this audit rules out less (2.03 to 0.00 as the training radius grows), while membership inference against robust models is reported to succeed MORE often (Song, Shokri and Mittal, arXiv:1905.10291). A lower number from this audit is therefore not evidence of less leakage.
